findings.failureScenario: A retained watcher whose subscriber stops draining continues to merge every distinct changed path into its BTreeSet. Neither that set nor raw notify ingress has a capacity or overflow transition, so a large tree churn can consume memory until process pressure or restart.
findings.action: Cap pending distinct paths per subscriber, replace excess with one explicit rescan/overflow state, & expose dropped-path count in watcher metrics.

findings.failureScenario: The macOS FSEvents callback sends every raw batch into an unbounded Worker channel. Worker drains at most 4,096 messages before expensive handling; a disk-change burst that outpaces handling leaves arbitrary batches queued, making memory growth proportional to outage or churn duration instead of a declared bound.
findings.action: Use bounded/coalescing ingress keyed by roots, turn saturation into a persisted full-rescan requirement, & expose queue depth, drops, and rescan state through Index status.

findings.failureScenario: Unix explicitly has no connection cap, accept_loop creates one OS thread per admitted socket, then each thread can block indefinitely waiting for its first hello frame. A same-user stalled client or reconnect storm can therefore exhaust threads and descriptors before service logic records a ConnectionOpened event or can recover through normal handoff.
findings.action: Apply a cross-platform admission semaphore before spawning, enforce a server-side hello/read deadline, & surface rejected/saturated/idle connection counts in service status or journal events.

findings.failureScenario: Every EngineClient or EngineSupervisor event subscriber receives an unbounded std::sync::mpsc queue. A live subscriber that stops reading remains sendable, so dispatch keeps cloning unsolicited sidecar frames into its backlog; failed sends prune only disconnected receivers. During high-rate engine output this creates unbounded retained JSON and no supervisor status field identifies pressure.
findings.action: Use bounded subscriber queues with explicit overflow/disconnect policy, retain one loss/resync marker per slow subscriber, & publish subscriber/backlog/overflow metrics with lifecycle status.
